Published online:
    September 4, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Asia — Nepal (Trishuli River valley), Tibet (China)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [NO]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    A glacial collapse on Nepal's Trishuli River on August 26 triggered a catastrophic ice/rock/mud slide killing 1,252+ people, leaving 4,200+ missing, and trapping ~900 workers across six hydropower tunnel projects. Nine days later, two workers were rescued alive from the Upper Trishuli 3A station. Infrastructure losses are estimated at ~$2.56B. International rescue teams from India, South Korea, China, and Australia are on the ground. Rebuilding ~20,000 homes is required.

    Relevance: NO — This is a regional humanitarian and infrastructure disaster in Nepal/Tibet with no direct linkage to US macro variables, rates, or equity pricing.
